newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 10.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 10.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - French advertising group Publicis says it has been awarded the advertising budget for Thomson Multimedia in France and Europe following a pitch against Ogilvy & Mather, McCann Erickson, Young & Rubicam, Grey and J.Walter Thomson.

NEW YORK - Sony Corp of America says it has entered into a marketing pact with the National Basketball Association that makes Sony an "Official Sponsor of the NBA." Financial details of the deal are not disclosed, but in a statement, Sony calls it an "expansive, multi-year alliance," and says it is the company's largest sports sponsorship yet.
PARIS - Jean-Claude Boulet, co-chairman of French advertising group Boulet Dru Dupuy Petit (BDDP), says his group is looking at rationalising its activities but says a takeover is not in the cards.

LONDON - Western International Media Europe, a British-based media-buying group, announces it has expanded operations and has a new presence in the Netherlands after taking a minority stake in Media Independent, a media specialist in Amsterdam.
SEATTLE - Golf star Greg Norman signs a seven-year, multimillion-dollar deal to be an "ambassador" for Boeing and its new line of business jets.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

REDMOND, Washington - Microsoft Corp expands its foray into the cable television business with a $1 billion investment in Philadelphia's Comcast Corp one of the biggest U.S. cable operators. Microsoft Chairman Bill Gates describes the deal as a chance to further the software giant's interest in providing multimedia services for home users.

REDWOOD CITY, California - Sales of goods and services used to build and access the Internet will top $100 billion by the year 2000, nearly triple sales of $34.97 billion in 1996, according to Zona Research.

PARIS - The first test of whether France's disputed language law applies to the Internet ended in fiasco when a court threw out the case. Two state-approved watchdogs promoting the use of the French language filed a complaint against the U.S. Georgia Institute of Technology's French campus for using English only on its website.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LONDON - A growing number of British companies are launching new products, after shying away from that business strategy since the last recession, experts say. Developing new consumer products is expensive and prone to failure, but an increasing number of British firms now think it is a risk worth taking.
SINGAPORE - Philips Electronics NV is seeing strong sales of its cellular phones in China with an estimated five to 10 percent of market share, a senior official says.
AMSTERDAM - Dutch brewer Heineken NV says its joint venture Asia Pacific Breweries has obtained a permit to do business in India.
JAKARTA Indonesia says that Japanese officials have asked for a cut in import tariffs on automobiles brought into the country and that the proposal is being studied. *********
STOCKHOLM - Swedish automotive group AB Volvo says it will stop sponsoring the show jumping and dressage world cups at the end of next season.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

SYDNEY - The Western world's penchant for recycling has produced such huge mountains of unsold waste that markets in used paper, plastic and bottles have collapsed. Prices have fallen so far in the past year that in its latest deal with Indonesia, Australia's A$100 ($76.09) million-per-year recycling industry may actually be paying Indonesia to accept its refuse. *********

VIENNA - Asian countries, with booming populations and low market shares in a traditionally tea-drinking region, are catching the eye of the international coffee industry with their potential for demand growth, coffee industry experts say.
VALLETTA - Tourist visitors to Malta rose by three percent in the first four months of this year, to 276,594 compared with the same period last year, the Office of Statistics says.
